name: Western Interdisciplinary Research Building
summary: Western Interdisciplinary Research Building is a seven-storey glazed slab with pale side panels interrupted by tall blue glass slots, set above a dark recessed ground storey and paired with a lower perpendicular east wing.

evidence.note: regional-2m surface minus local ground: median 33.46 m, 90th percentile 37.6 m, maximum 38.91 m.
Western Facilities Management exterior photograph; masonry, trim and opening proportions assessed against the orthophoto.
Exposed pale slab edge with irregular blue vertical glazed slots and a deep glazed setback at grade. Construction sheeting appears at the top in this older frame.
Street-facing end is a tall glass grid, with fine vertical divisions and differing horizontal spandrels.
Finished glass at grade wraps the corner below the overhanging opaque facade.
Tall slab along the southwest approach intersects a lower east wing. Local roof samples separate the 37 m and 16 m plateaus.
PIL mean wall or glazing sample, source-pixel rectangle (x, y, width, height) (251, 130, 4, 4) gives #9c9b97.
Slots end well above the undercroft on the side facing the road. The finished university photo shows continuous lower glazing on the end wall and stronger horizontal spandrels only higher up.
The pale side plane projects over a shadowed, recessed ground floor. Narrow framing returns toward the glazed end.

Across the slab and wing, shifting the plan roughly 5 m west and 3 m south fits 1 m roof returns better. The long occupied slab returns 37–39 m and the rear service court about 32 m. The broad exposed roof is light in the 2025 photograph.

parts.name: Recessed glazed base of high block

notes: Vision glass and opaque glass alternate in unequal vertical strips. At grade the glazed volume recedes behind the overhanging side wall.
